name: Cranial Nerve and Nuclear Aplasia

criteria.description: Congenital absence or severe hypoplasia of one or more cranial nerve nuclei confirmed by imaging or histopathology
Clinical evidence of congenital cranial nerve palsies corresponding to absent nuclei
Exclusion of acquired causes such as trauma, infection, or neoplasm
MRI demonstrating absence or hypoplasia of cranial nerve nuclei and nerves
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with cranial nerve development (if available)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital cranial nerve palsies with imaging or histopathologic confirmation of absent or hypoplastic cranial nerve nuclei and exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by neuroimaging; genetic testing may aid but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital unilateral or bilateral facial nerve palsy
searchTerms: one or both sides facial nerve weakness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or severely reduced gag reflex due to glossopharyngeal and vagus nerve nuclear aplasia
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to nerve problems

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital ophthalmoplegia related to oculomotor and trochlear nerve nuclear aplasia

common.symptomName: Dysphagia secondary to multiple cranial nerve involvement
searchTerms: swallowing problems due to multiple nerve issues

common.symptomName: Hypotonia of facial and pharyngeal muscles
searchTerms: low muscle tone in face and throat
reduced muscle strength in face and throat
poor sucking or swallowing in neonates

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to impaired vagal nerve function
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to vagus nerve

occasional.symptomName: Hearing impairment from cochlear nerve involvement
searchTerms: impaired hearing due to cochlear nerve

occasional.symptomName: Ptosis due to levator palpebrae superioris muscle paralysis

searchTerms: episodes of low breathing at night

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones related to cranial nerve dysfunction

rare.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction including abnormal heart rate variability
Facial synkinesis due to aberrant nerve regeneration
searchTerms: involuntary facial movements after nerve injury

imaging: MRI showing absent or hypoplastic cranial nerve nuclei
MRI demonstrating absent or hypoplastic cranial nerves
genetic: Variants in genes regulating cranial nerve development (e.g., HOX genes, PHOX2B) may be identified
other: Electrophysiological studies showing absent or reduced cranial nerve function

distinguishingFeatures: Congenital facial and abducens nerve palsy with limb abnormalities
Normal cranial nerve nuclei on imaging

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties with aspiration risk
